questions.question: Which is the first state to receive rain from the Monsoon in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Kerala is the first state in India to receive rainfall from the** Southwest Monsoon.**
 
• This is because the **Arabian Sea branch** of the monsoon first hits the **Western Ghats of Kerala.**
 
• Kerala has a** tropical monsoon climate**, characterized by a lengthy rainy season that extends from **June to September.**
 
• The monsoon season in India typically lasts from **June to September.** 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• The **monsoon season in India has two parts**: the **Southwest monsoon **and the **North-East monsoon.**
 
• The Southwest monsoon brings rain to most of the country, while the **northeast monsoon** brings rain to parts of** southern India.** 
 
• The monsoon brings the most rain to **western and central India**, where it accounts for over **90%** of the annual rainfall.
 
• In **southern and northwestern** India, the monsoon accounts for **50–75%** of the annual rainfall. 
 
• The monsoon is caused by **moist winds** from the southwest that are drawn up from the oceans. 
 
• The monsoon blows from the northeast during the cooler months and reverses direction to blow from the southwest during the warmer months.

questions.question: The season for torrential downpours, often accompanied by hail, associated with violent winds, and localized thunderstorms. In West Bengal, these kinds of storms are known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kaal Baisakhi**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kaal Baisakhi** is the term used in **West Bengal** for the violent thunderstorms that occur during the **pre-monsoon season**.
 
• This phenomenon is characterized by **torrential downpours, often accompanied by hail, violent winds, and localized thunderstorms**.
 
• These storms typically occur in the months of **April and May** and are known for their sudden and severe nature.
 
• The name **"Kaal Baisakhi"** translates to "**Calamity of the month of Baisakh**" (**April-May**) in Bengali.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kaal Baisakhi** is a localized weather event and is part of the broader weather patterns influenced by the South Asian climate.
 
• These storms are crucial for the **agricultural sector** in the region, providing much-needed rainfall for crops.
 
• However, due to their intensity, they can also cause significant damage to property and agriculture.
 
• Similar weather phenomena are observed in other parts of India and are known by different names, such as **"Nor'westers"** in **Assam **and **Odisha**.

questions.question: Which of the following is a rare species as per International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Asiatic buffalo**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• International Union for Conservation of Nature:

 
 
• IUCN is a membership Union uniquely composed of both government and civil society organizations.
 
• Created in 1948, it is the global authority on the status of the natural world and the measures needed to safeguard it.
 
• Julian Huxley is the founder of the International Union for Conservation of Nature.
 
• It is headquartered in Switzerland.
 
• The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species is the world's most comprehensive inventory of the global conservation status of plant and animal species.
 
• It uses a set of quantitative criteria to evaluate the extinction risk of species. These criteria are relevant to most species and all regions of the world.
 
• The IUCN Red List Categories define the extinction risk of species assessed. 
 
 
• Nine categories extend from NE (Not Evaluated) to EX (Extinct). Critically Endangered (CR), Endangered (EN), and Vulnerable (VU) species are considered to be threatened with extinction.
 
 
 
• It is recognized as the most authoritative guide to the status of biological diversity.
 
• The first international red data books were published in 1966.
 
• ​International Union for Conservation of Nature is founded on 5th October 1948.
 
 
 
• **Asiatic buffalo​**
 
 
• The Asian buffalo, also known as the wild Asian buffalo and the Asiatic buffalo.
 
• It is a giant bovine that is indigenous to Southeast Asia and the Indian subcontinent.
 
• Asia's tropical and subtropical jungles are home to water buffalo.
 
• Since they spend most of their time in the water, their comment is perfect.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://encrypted-tbn3.gstatic.com/images?q=tbn:ANd9GcRMp3wWY5-Gmrk-luOQqmhxqSmtpzOUcqZ29PRzRXdNL64UU4BL] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Lion-tailed macaque 

 
 
• The Lion-tailed macaque (Macaca silenus) is recognized as endangered species in India.
 
• It is endemic to the Western Ghats of South India.
 
• The hair of the lion-tailed macaque is black. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://encrypted-tbn1.gstatic.com/images?q=tbn:ANd9GcQ8dQrMjOFGM4oMIm5oClSA3ABgGMjhu2o1SZ9lJhBwwAmfwJn6] 

 
• **Blue sheep**

 
 
• ​Blue sheep is also called **Bhara.** 
 
• Despite their name, blue sheep are neither blue nor sheep. 
 
• It's scientific name is Pseudois nayaur.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/f/fe/Bharal_-_Shreeram_M_V_-_Kibber%2C_Spiti_Valley%2C_Himachal_Pradesh%2C_India.jpg] 

 
• Gangetic Dolphin:

 
 
• The Gangetic river dolphins can only live in freshwater, are blind and catch their prey in a unique manner, using ultrasonic sound waves.
 
• They are distributed across seven states in India: Assam, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Bihar, Jharkhand and West Bengal.
 
• Categorized as ‘Endangered’ on the International Union for the Conservation of Nature’s (IUCN) Red List.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/8/81/Ganges_River_Dolphin_cropped.jpg]

questions.question: Which of the following statements about climate is INCORRECT?

options.text: ‘Monsoon’ type of climate is found mainly in south and southeast Asia.
India’s climate has characteristics of tropical as well as subtropical climates.
Coastal areas of India experience less contrasts in temperature conditions as compared to the interior of the country.
India experiences comparatively stronger winters as compared to central Asia.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**India experiences comparatively stronger winters as compared to central Asia.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Monsoon** type of climate is found mainly in south and southeast Asia.
 
• India's climate has characteristics of **tropical as well as subtropical climates**.
 
• Coastal areas of India experience **less contrasts in temperature conditions** as compared to the interior of the country.
 
• Central Asia experiences stronger winters compared to India due to its continental climate, which is characterized by more extreme seasonal temperature variations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• India's climate is significantly influenced by the **Himalayas and the Thar Desert**, which moderate the temperature and create monsoon conditions.
 
• The Himalayas act as a barrier to the frigid katabatic winds flowing down from Central Asia, keeping most of the Indian subcontinent warmer than most locations at similar latitudes.
 
• The **Thar Desert** plays a crucial role in attracting the moisture-laden southwest summer monsoon winds that bring most of India's rainfall during the year.
 
• India's diverse climate ranges from the **tropical climate** in the south to a more temperate climate in the north, and alpine in the higher Himalayan regions.

questions.question: According to Koeppen's Scheme of classification of climate, which of the following characteristics is associated with 'Group E'?

options.text: The average temperature for all months is below 10°C
The average temperature of the coldest month is 18°C or higher
The average temperature of the coldest month is –3°C or below
The average temperature of the coldest month is higher than –3°C but below 18°C

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The average temperature for all months is below 10ºC**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The average temperature for all months is below 10ºC** is the characteristic associated with 'Group E' in Koeppen's Scheme of classification of climate.
 
• Koeppen's classification is a widely used system for categorizing the world's climates based on the annual and monthly averages of temperature and precipitation.
 
• 'Group E' represents polar climates, which are characterized by extremely low temperatures throughout the year.
 
• These climates are typically found in the polar regions, including Antarctica and the Arctic.
 
• Due to the harsh conditions, these regions have very limited vegetation and are often covered in ice and snow.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Koeppen's Scheme** was developed by Wladimir Koeppen, a German climatologist, in the early 20th century.
 
• The classification system divides the world into five main climate groups: A (tropical), B (dry), C (temperate), D (continental), and E (polar).
 
• Each group is further divided based on specific criteria related to temperature and precipitation patterns.
 
• Koeppen's classification is still widely used in climatology, geography, and environmental studies due to its simplicity and effectiveness in describing climate zones.

questions.question: Which of the following factors is NOT responsible for the loss of fertility of agricultural land?

options.text: Higher cation exchange capacity of soil

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Higher cation exchange capacity of soil.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Soil fertility** decline occurs when the quantities of nutrients removed from the soil in harvested products exceed the quantities of nutrients being applied.
 
• The nutrient requirements of the crop are met from soil reserves until these reserves cannot meet crop demands.
 
• This results in a reduction of plant growth and yield.
 
• **Nutrients may be removed from the soil by:**
 
 
• Growing extensive crops
 
• Soil erosion
 
• Leaching.
 
• Alkalisation of soil
 
• Salinisation of soil
 
• Waterlogging
 
 
 
• **Higher cation exchange **usually indicates more clay and organic matter is present in the soil, high CEC soils generally have greater water holding capacity than low CEC soils.
 
• **Hence Higher cation exchange capacity of soil is NOT responsible for the loss of fertility of agricultural land.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Fertility can be maintained with the maintenance** of soil organic matter, soil structure, soil nutrient status and satisfactory soil pH.**
 
• This can be achieved in cropping systems by:
 
 
• including pasture phases and leguminous crops
 
• including the addition of soil amendments or fertilisers
 
• employing a reduced tillage system
 
• retaining crop residues on site.

questions.question: Sal, acacia, and bamboo, which are types of Dry Tropical Forest, receive what amount of annual rainfall?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Dry Tropical Forests** are characterized by a** long dry season **and a** short rainy season**.

• These forests receive an **annual rainfall** ranging from** 51 cm to 151 cm**, which is **lower** than the rainfall received by other forest types.

• **The Indian Forest Act, 1927** considered it a **tree**. Accordingly, cutting bamboo from outside forests and transporting it was made unlawful.
 
• **In 2017 **an amendment was made to the Indian Forest Act, 1927 and bamboo has been **removed from the tree category.**

questions.question: What type of forests are found north and south of the equator between 40° and 60° where rainfall is high, between 500-1500 mm in a year?

• **Temperate deciduous forests** are found between **40° and 60° north and south of the equator.**
 
• The** rainfall is high, between 500-1,500 mm **a year.
 
• The temperatures remain on average **above 0°C even in the winter.**
 
• The **summer temperatures **average between **25-20°C.**
 
• The winter is cooler, encouraging the trees to shed their leaves.

• **Taiga** is generally referred to in **North America as a boreal forest or snow forest.**
 
• Taiga is the terrestrial biome with the **lowest annual average temperatures.**
 
• **The total yearly precipitation in the taiga biome is 10 - 30 inches (25 - 75 cm).**
 
• Snow may remain on the ground for as long as nine months in the northernmost extensions of the taiga biome.

**Coniferous forests**

 
• **Coniferous forests consist mostly of conifers**.
 
• The average temperature in **winter ranges from -40°C (-40°F) to 20°C (68°F).**
 
• The **average summer temperatures** are usually around **10°C (50°F).**
 
• **Precipitation** in coniferous forests varies from** 300 to 900 mm annually.**

**Mediterranean forests**

 
• **Mediterranean forests, **woodlands, and scrub is a biome defined by the World Wide Fund for Nature.
 
• **Precipitation totals ranging from 35 to 90 cm.**
 
• Mediterranean climate experiences **22.0 °C during summer** and **18 and −3 °C during winter.**

questions.question: Which of the following states has mangrove forests?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Andhra Pradesh**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Andhra Pradesh** is one of the states in India that has mangrove forests.
 
• Mangrove forests are coastal ecosystems found in tropical and subtropical regions, characterized by salt-tolerant trees and shrubs.
 
• These forests play a crucial role in protecting coastal areas from erosion, storm surges, and maintaining biodiversity.
 
• Andhra Pradesh has significant mangrove cover, particularly in the Godavari and Krishna delta regions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The other options listed do not have mangrove forests. For instance, **Manipur** is a landlocked state, and **Telangana** and **Rajasthan** do not have coastal regions conducive for mangrove ecosystems.
 
• Mangroves are vital for the environment as they provide habitat for various species, support fisheries, and help in carbon sequestration.
 
• Conservation efforts are essential to protect these unique ecosystems from threats like deforestation, pollution, and climate change.
 
• In India, mangrove forests are also found in other states such as West Bengal (Sundarbans), Odisha, Tamil Nadu, and Gujarat.

• Found in the areas of coasts influenced by tides. Mud and silt get accumulated on such coasts.
 
• Dense mangroves are the common varieties with roots of the plants submerged underwater.
 
• The deltas of the Ganga, the Mahanadi, the Krishana, the Godavari, and the Kaveri are covered by such vegetation.
 
• In the Ganga Brahmaputra delta, Sundari trees are found, which provide durable hard timber.
 
• Palm, coconut, keora, agar, also grow in some parts of the delta.
 
• Royal Bengal Tiger is the famous animal in these forests. Turtles, crocodiles, gharials, and snakes are also found in these forests.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**__Tropical Evergreen Forests:__

 
• These forests are restricted to heavy rainfall areas of the *Western Ghats and the island groups of Lakshadweep, Andaman, and Nicobar, upper parts of Assam, and Tamil Nadu coast.*
 
• They are at their best in areas having more than 200 cm of rainfall with a short dry season.
 
• The trees reach great heights up to 60 meters or even above.
 
• Since the region is warm and wet throughout the year, it has luxuriant vegetation of all kinds.
 
• The trees, shrubs, and creepers give it a multilayered structure.
 
• There is no definite time for trees to shed their leaves.
 
• As such, these forests appear green all the year-round

Tropical Deciduous Forests

 
• ​These are the most widespread forests of India.
 
• They are also called the monsoon forests and spread over the region receiving rainfall between 200 cm and 70 cm.
 
• Trees of this forest type shed their leaves for about six to eight weeks in dry summer.
 
• On the basis of the availability of water, these forests are further divided into moist and dry deciduous.

Natural vegetation refers to a plant community, which has grown naturally without human aid and has been left undisturbed by humans for a long time. The following major types of vegetation may be identified in our country

 
• Tropical Evergreen Forests
 
• Tropical Deciduous Forests
 
• Tropical Thorn Forests and Scrubs
 
• Montane Forests
 
• Mangrove Forests

questions.question: Which of the following is the most widespread forest type in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tropical Deciduous Forests**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tropical deciduous forests,** also referred to as **monsoon forests,** thrive in regions receiving an annual rainfall ranging from 70 to 200 cm.
 
• These forests exhibit lush greenery and dense vegetation during the wet summer months but transform during the dry winters, characterized by leaf shedding and a drier landscape.
 
• Found in regions such as India, northern Australia, and central America, tropical deciduous forests are particularly widespread in India, covering vast areas including Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Orissa, and parts of Maharashtra.
 
• In India, these forests hold significant economic importance as they serve as abundant sources of valuable timber species like teak, sal, sandalwood, and rosewood.
 
• These trees are extensively utilized in the lumber industry for various purposes such as construction, railway infrastructure, and furniture manufacturing. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Littoral and swamp forests, commonly referred to as wetland forests, thrive in coastal regions, along seashores, creeks, river estuaries, and deltas. They can also be observed at the edges of swampy islands and along sandy beaches.
 
• **Tropical thorn forests, **characterized by scrub-like vegetation, are typically found in desert regions. These forests are prevalent in tropical and subtropical areas and thrive in semi-arid regions receiving less than 70 cm of annual rainfall.
 
• **Montane ecosystems** are situated on mountain slopes, where the alpine climate significantly influences the ecosystem. As elevation increases, temperatures drop, leading to distinct stratification within the ecosystem due to varying environmental conditions.
